name: learned_recovery_v5_deferred_direction
purpose: LearnedRecovery-v4 implements forward and reverse ejection with separate actors, so identifying the held-out mechanism reduces to noticing which actor moved. The shortcut audit confirms this: a one-frame model and a hand-written motion rule both match the recurrent model exactly. V5 uses one ejector per cube for both directions and defers the direction-bearing force by a per-episode delay, so early frames are uninformative about direction.
changes_from_v4: one shared ejector per cube replaces the separate forward and reverse sweepers
an axial approach force identical across directions
a lateral direction force applied only after a per-episode delay
delay drawn uniformly from [10, 34) so no fixed decision step is correct
unchanged_from_v4: task, reward, protected-object constraint, blockage mechanisms

physics_smoke_gate.note: Frozen before the smoke runs. Failing any check means V5 is not used.

ladder_prediction.note: Recorded before the audit runs, so the outcome cannot be reframed.
ladder_prediction.expected: Rung 2 held-out accuracy falls well below rung 4. If it does not, the shortcut is not caused by separate actors and this diagnosis is wrong.
ladder_prediction.falsifies_the_diagnosis_if: rung 2 remains statistically indistinguishable from rung 4

claim_boundary: A benchmark-construction change only. No recovery, routing, or method claim follows until the ladder and a closed-loop evaluation are run.
